title: Kestrel and the Visitor
premise: When her twin brother dies under circumstances no one will explain, Silas Eriksen returns to their grandmother's isolated farmhouse to settle the estate and bury him properly. But the house remembers things it shouldn't: photographs sprout an extra chair, doors refuse to stay counted, and a presence that has fed on the Eriksen line for generations begins making itself visible to her. Silas learns that survival in this family was always a transaction—one twin hidden, one twin offered—and that her grandmother's 'inheritance' is a debt now due. To save her found family of neighbors who refuse to abandon her, Silas must lead them out before the harvest moon completes the count, ending with her choosing to stay behind as the offering so the others cross the property line alive.
about_author: Juniper Vasquez is the pen name of a former rural hospice nurse who spent a decade listening to deathbed confessions in farm country, stories that now haunt her fiction. She writes horror about houses that keep accounts, and lives—she insists—somewhere with very good locks.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She arrives at the farmhouse for her twin Wren's funeral, stunned to learn the body was misidentified—it isn't Wren at all. The county can't explain it; the casket holds a stranger wearing Wren's face. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread as Silas realizes someone, or something, came home in her brother's place.

chapters.title: Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Sorting grandma's effects, Silas finds decades of journals obsessively counting doors, chairs, names. That night every door in the house stands open by exactly one. The neighbors—the Halvorsens, who've farmed beside the Eriksens for generations—warn her not to stay past dark. Beat: isolation sharpening into paranoia.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Old family photographs begin including a chair that was never there—a high-backed seat positioned where Wren used to sit. When Silas photographs the photos, the chair appears closer each time. Mrs. Halvorsen goes pale and burns her own copy of a shared picture. Beat: the horror becomes undeniable and contagious.

chapters.title: What Grandma Kept
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with a flashback chapter from grandmother Astrid's 1974 journal. Astrid bargained with something in the orchard after a blizzard killed half the family: one hidden, one given, harvest moon to harvest moon. The current count is overdue because Wren ran instead of paying. Beat: inheritance revealed as predation.

chapters.title: The Halvorsen Debt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Silas and teenage Petra Halvorsen. Petra confesses her family has served as 'witnesses' for three generations—bound to watch, forbidden to warn. Petra breaks the rule anyway, telling Silas how the count works: everyone the house knows by name must be out by moonrise or added. Beat: found family forming against the rules.

chapters.title: Wren, Maybe
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A figure matching Wren appears at the orchard fence, asking to be let in, knowing childhood secrets—but its shadow sits in the extra chair. Silas tests it with a memory only the real Wren would falsify correctly, and it passes perfectly, which is worse. Beat: hope weaponized into terror.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV across the Halvorsen household. The thing stops hiding: lights fail, the road out loops back on itself, and every mirror shows one more person than the room holds. The Halvorsens decide to defy their covenant and help Silas evacuate rather than witness another payment. Beat: solidarity against escalating supernatural siege.

chapters.title: The Orchard Bargain
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confronts the presence at the orchard's heart—an old, patient hunger wearing Astrid's voice—demanding terms. It offers a trade: any named soul willingly left behind settles the debt and releases the rest. It shows her Wren, alive, held since spring. Beat: the price of survival made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon
chapters.summary: Split POV: Silas inside the house, Petra counting heads at the property line. Under the rising moon, Silas loads the Halvorsens into the truck, lies that she'll follow, and turns back for Wren—who begs her to run. She gives her name freely instead. Climax: the count completes, the chair fills, the moon crests.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Count
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, then Silas's epilogue-voice journal entry. The truck crosses the line as the house exhales; Wren stumbles out of the orchard at dawn, hollow but breathing, freed by his sister's substitution. Months later, Petra receives a letter in Silas's handwriting, postmarked nowhere, counting doors. Final beat: survival's cost endures, but so does the family it bought.
